name: MercadoLibre
thesis: LatAm e-commerce + fintech compounder currently in a deliberate investment cycle — deepening logistics moat (same/next-day shipments, 1P, free shipping) to widen distance from Shopee and Amazon, while the Mercado Pago credit / acquiring flywheel scales. Margin compression in 2026 is acceptable while engagement metrics (items per buyer, same/next-day volume) prove the investment is producing returns.
key_driver: Logistics-moat investment ROI: must show as engagement metrics accelerating while margin compresses

tier_1_kpis.name: GMV Growth (FXN)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Brazil GMV FXN growth <20% for 2 consecutive Qs (the moat market)

tier_1_kpis.name: Items Sold per Unique Active Buyer
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Declines YoY for 2 consecutive Qs (engagement breaking)

tier_1_kpis.name: Same/Next-Day Shipments YoY
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: <15% YoY (logistics-moat investment failing to drive throughput)

tier_1_kpis.name: Acquiring TPV Growth (FXN)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: <25%, OR instore TPV decelerating faster than online

tier_1_kpis.name: Operating Margin
tier_1_kpis.current: 10.1% Q4'25 (9.0% ex-$99M Brazilian tax credit); FY ~11.1%
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: <8% for 2 consecutive Qs WITHOUT engagement metrics improving (this is the investment-justification gate — sub-8% is acceptable if engagement KPIs above keep accelerating; if they stall, it becomes a break)
tier_1_kpis.notes: Margin compression is explicit in MELI's own deck p.20: 'The margin compression reflects our decision to invest in key long-term growth opportunities.'

tier_1_kpis.name: Credit NPL 90d+
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: >9% (credit risk import from credit-card portfolio expansion)

nuance.bear_case: The 'deliberate investment' framing may mask structurally lower-margin categories. 1P commerce, subsidized shipping, and credit cards are inherently lower-return businesses than the marketplace flywheel. If MELI is buying GMV growth with margin, the compounding thesis weakens — revenue without earnings power expansion. Credit-card expansion also imports NPL risk at scale.
nuance.adversarial_take: Investment thesis (Shopee/Amazon defense) is YOUR working hypothesis — MELI's deck only says 'long-term growth opportunities' generically; competitive framing is not validated by management commentary. Watch for explicit Shopee/Amazon mentions in subsequent earnings calls to either confirm or refute the framing.
nuance.stress_test: If Brazil GMV FXN decelerates while Shopee continues taking share AND items/buyer flatlines, the 'investment is working' framing collapses → margin compression becomes structural, not strategic, and verdict moves to Broken.

competitive_watchlist: Mercado Pago competitors (NU Pagamentos, PicPay, etc.)
thesis_breakers_qualitative: Brazil GMV FXN growth <20% for 2 consecutive Qs
Items per buyer flatlining or declining
Op margin sub-8% for 2 Qs WITHOUT engagement metrics accelerating
Explicit competitive concession in management commentary about Shopee/Amazon share losses
working_hypotheses: Investment cycle is specifically Shopee/Amazon defensive (NOT validated by deck commentary; awaiting transcript confirmation)
Credit-card expansion is the primary near-term margin drag rather than free shipping
